text:
Passive movements are joint movements produced entirely by an external force, such as a therapist, a machine, or the patient's other limb, while the patient's own muscles stay relaxed. In physiotherapy they maintain range of motion, reduce stiffness, and assess joint mobility, and they differ from active movement (the patient moves alone) and active-assisted movement (the patient contributes with help). The team note's claim about ancient Greek gymnastics is something I can't verify, and it doesn't match how the term is used clinically, so I'd leave it out.

CONFIDENCE: 90
